security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU raises an illegal-instruction exception when guest reads an hpmcounter CSR whose corresponding mhpmevent register is set to an unimplemented event selector (ill-configured), instead of returning a constant zero value
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: riscv_pmu_ctr_ctrl OR riscv_hpmcounter_read OR counter_get_ops: trap path for access to CSR where event selector is invalid/unsupported but the counter CSR index itself is implemented
security_spec.summary: Spec 2539 removes the trap allowance for ill-configured counters — if QEMU still raises #I for reads of counters programmed to unrecognized events, compliant guests expecting a silent constant return will fault, causing host-visible guest crash

findings.finding: Predicate checks only pmu_avail_ctrs (counter index availability), not mhpmevent validity. Does NOT raise illegal-instruction for counters that exist but have invalid mhpmevent programming. Correctly gates access only on counter-index existence.
M-mode counter predicate likewise checks only pmu_avail_ctrs for counter-index availability. No mhpmevent-validity check. Does NOT trap on ill-configured counters.

For counters not mapped to cycles or instructions (i.e. ill-configured), falls into else branch returning ctr_val (0 after reset). Always returns RISCV_EXCP_NONE — no illegal-instruction trap. Compliant with spec: returns zero/current-value instead of raising exception.

Ignores return value of riscv_pmu_update_event_map(). CSR write always succeeds even if event selector is invalid/unsupported, which is correct spec behavior — writing unsupported event selectors is legal, counter just won't count.

Returns -1 for unsupported raw events (default case in switch). This correctly prevents counter increments but does NOT cause any exception — the CSR write path ignores this return. Ill-configured counters silently return their static value (0).

Only increments counters whose event_idx is in cpu->pmu_event_ctr_map. Ill-configured counters (event_idx not in the map) will never be incremented, keeping their value at the static/written value (effectively zero). No exception raised — correct behavior.
Delegates to riscv_pmu_read_ctr which never returns an exception. CSR index computation is correct (handles both M-mode and S-mode counter ranges). No trap path for ill-configured counters.
